title: Podiatry: specialist foot care
intro: Podiatrists are specialists in foot care. They treat nails, corns, calluses and foot problems, and help people with diabetes or circulation problems prevent serious foot complications. Regular professional care can protect mobility and independence, especially in people at higher risk.

sections.heading: What podiatrists do
paragraphs: Podiatrists assess the feet, trim nails, remove thickened skin and corns, treat ingrown nails and warts, fit padding and insoles, advise on footwear and educate about daily foot care. Medical foot care usually means treating feet affected by disease, such as diabetes or nerve damage.

sections.heading: Who benefits most
paragraphs: People with diabetes who have nerve damage, poor circulation or previous foot ulcers have the highest risk of wounds that heal poorly and can become infected. Older people with difficulty reaching their feet, people with fungal or deformed nails, rheumatoid arthritis or severe foot deformities also benefit.

sections.heading: What you can do at home
paragraphs: Look at your feet daily, including soles and between the toes, or ask someone to help. Wash with lukewarm water, dry thoroughly, apply moisturiser but not between the toes, cut nails straight across, wear well-fitting shoes and clean, seamless socks, and never walk barefoot. Do not use sharp tools, strong chemicals or hot water bottles on feet with reduced sensation.

sections.heading: Footwear and aids
paragraphs: Shoes should be roomy in the toe area, with good support and no pressure points. Insoles, padding or custom shoes may be prescribed for high-risk feet. Check inside shoes for objects before putting them on. Replace worn shoes.

sections.heading: When to seek help quickly
paragraphs: Seek urgent advice for a blister, wound, redness, swelling, warmth, a colour change or fever, especially in people with diabetes. Foot problems can progress rapidly. Ask your doctor whether you qualify for podiatry care under your health insurance, as rules differ.

examples.title: Daily foot check
examples.text: Imagine you have diabetes and reduced feeling in your feet. You could examine your feet each evening with a mirror, and call your doctor if you notice a blister or red area.

examples.title: Choosing shoes
examples.text: Suppose you need new shoes. You might shop in the afternoon when feet are slightly swollen, check the width, and ask the podiatrist for advice.
